items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: Yeah, Francois Mosley's band. ... Fred Howard on alto.

ctx.x: Oh, I wanted to ask you about Frankie Halfpaint Jackson. You made a record with him, huh? Oh, yeah. I made a record with him. You remember who was in that band?

Yeah, Francois Mosley's band. Charlie Ducasse, myself, Fred Reed on piano. And Charlie Ducasse on guitar and that boy, Lil Sax on tenor. Fred Howard on alto. He played alto on clarinet. And what else? Fred on piano, me on trumpet. Al Wynn on trombone. Al Wynn. I got a letter from him the other day. Little Sax's name is what? Robert Crowder. Everybody called him. You know who he was, Kenta? Y'all didn't know Cecil. He used to play with Earl Hein.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: A big stout fellow played clarinet and saxophone named Fred Howard... I was on the trumpet... And we had Al Wins a lot of different times.

ctx.x: Who was in the band ready to go to the world?

Well, a fellow on guitar named Charles Ducasten. A big stout fellow played clarinet and saxophone named Fred Howard. And Fred Reeves on the piano. I was on the trumpet. Francois was on the drums. And we had Al Wins a lot of different times. Now, I'll tell you who worked with us there a long time. People would not believe that, but it's true. You heard of Ted Wilson? Oh, yeah. Well, he worked right there with us a long time after he left his dorm. Oh, no. Did you know that band from Kansas City? A fellow that died…
I don't know anything about that. Ted did.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: And he had Lawrence Brown on tenor, Robert Crowder on tenor, Fred Howard on alto and clarinet. And he had Clowns, Clowns Brown on piano. And he had me...

ctx.x: Well, Al Wynn was one. I was one. Francois and Duke El, Duke Caston. I mean, his name is Charles Duke Caston, but we called him Duke. And he had Lawrence Brown on tenor, Robert Crowder on tenor, Fred Howard on alto and clarinet. And he had Clowns, Clowns Brown on piano. He had me, I'm trying to think of these trumpet players now. I forget that boy's name. But I mean, I mean anyhow, well, Hopkin went off with us. Hopkin and me and another little young trumpet, he's younger than us, but he could play a lot and he…
You named the tuba player or bass player?
